name: Guardian Systems DermAlert DA-2 'Scarlet'
description:
The DermAlert DA-2 is Guardian Systems' dedicated dermal irritant spray, developed as a complement to their broader personal and institutional security product line. The active compound, GS-Urticant-2, is a synthetic urticant — a contact irritant that triggers mast cell degranulation and histamine cascade in exposed skin tissue, producing immediate intense inflammation, hive-like wheals, and a burning, crawling sensation that subjects consistently describe as unbearable within thirty seconds of exposure. Critically, GS-Urticant-2 is not a pain-channel agonist in the conventional sense — it does not activate TRPV1 channels and thus provides no cross-resistance with OC-tolerant individuals or those with pain-dampening chrome. The inflammatory response is immunological rather than neurological, bypassing most standard pain-tolerance augmentation.

The DA-2 is packaged in a distinctive red-and-black canister with a wide-fan nozzle optimized for sweeping deployment across crowds or through doorways. The compound produces a visible reddish aerosol mist — the product's 'Scarlet' designation — which serves a secondary purpose as a visual deterrent and crowd-movement indicator. GS-Urticant-2 settles on clothing and remains active for approximately two hours, meaning subjects cannot simply move away from the initial deployment area and expect relief — the compound travels with them.

Guardian markets the DA-2 heavily to Tier 2 and 3 venue security, transit security, and residential building security services as a step up from basic OC spray without the licensing burden of more restricted compounds. The product's effectiveness against augmented individuals has made it popular in environments where the security staff cannot reliably assess the augmentation status of potential threats.
legality: Legal — licensed security use; civilian ownership permitted with standard personal defense registration
specifications:
Active compound: GS-Urticant-2 (synthetic urticant, immunological irritant)
Delivery: wide-fan nozzle, 120-degree arc at 2.5m effective range
Onset: 20–30 seconds
Duration of effect: 45–90 minutes; clothing contamination active for up to 2 hours
Visible mist: red-tinted aerosol (secondary deterrent/indicator function)
Canister capacity: 8 bursts
Weight: 0.22 kg
Dimensions: 16cm × 5.5cm
Cross-resistance with OC: none (different mechanism)
Price: Φ95
tactical_use: Security teams deploy the DA-2 in doorway and corridor chokepoints, using the wide-fan nozzle to contaminate the full width of a passage and force crowd redirection. The two-hour clothing persistence means a single deployment creates a sustained deterrent zone that security can manage passively — anyone who passed through the contaminated area will be visibly affected and identifiable. In venue security, it is used to create exit-forcing pressure in crowd-management situations without requiring physical engagement. The red mist coloration allows operators to quickly identify which individuals in a crowd have passed through a deployment zone.
cultural_context: Guardian Red or Scarlet has a less fear-laden reputation than Arcturus products — it is associated with venue bouncers and transit security rather than riot police, and the visible red mist has become something of a visual shorthand in media and street art for 'security is here.' Getting 'Scarletted' at a venue is considered embarrassing rather than traumatic by most Tier 2-3 residents, a distinction that reflects the difference between professional security tool and state force instrument. Some venues have faced criticism for using it preemptively in situations that did not warrant it, leading to a Guardian-funded campaign emphasizing 'responsible deployment protocols.'
story_hooks: A Tier 3 transit hub security supervisor has been deploying DA-2 against specific individuals repeatedly — the pattern of targets suggests they are all connected to something the supervisor doesn't want anyone to see

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, aggressive canister with a distinctly utilitarian security aesthetic. The form factor suggests industrial efficiency—not elegant, but unmistakably purposeful. Wide-mouth nozzle dominates the top, splayed outward like a predator's maw. The overall impression is clinical and hostile.
physical_description.dimensions: 16cm tall × 5.5cm diameter (canister body); nozzle spreads to approximately 8cm width at the dispersal head
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light in hand—0.22kg makes it feel almost negligible, but the wide base and forward-weight nozzle create a subtle top-heavy bias that demands control. Feels like a precision tool despite its compact mass.
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminum pressure canister with aerospace-grade polymeric nozzle assembly. Internal bladder system for compound containment.
physical_description.finish: Matte black base with high-gloss crimson stripe running vertically down the primary face. Nozzle finished in satin gunmetal. Heavy machining marks visible on the canister seams—no effort at concealment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep matte black body with arterial-red accent stripe and chrome nozzle. Minimal branding in white sans-serif typeface.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip panel with fine knurling for retention even in sweaty or gloved hands. Slightly tacky to the touch—intentional for security use.
distinctive_features: Wide-fan nozzle with 120-degree dispersal angle—engineered for area coverage rather than precision
Pressure gauge indicator on upper canister (small translucent window showing charge level)
Burst-count mechanical counter (3-digit dial) mounted on grip—tracks deployments
Safety lever lock integrated into the trigger guard with audible detent click
Micro-etched serial number and Guardian Systems Φ logo on the canister shoulder
Faint residual red staining around the nozzle edges from manufacturing quality control tests
Thermal warning stripe on lower third that darkens if canister exceeds safe pressure threshold
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Guardian Systems corporate logo (shield with stylized Φ symbol) stamped in chrome on upper canister. 'DA-2 SCARLET' printed in white block letters across the matte-black face. Manufacturer address and hazard classifications in microscopic text along the base rim.
physical_description.condition_typical: Arrives in pristine condition from the factory, but in field use shows rapid cosmetic wear—scuffing on the grip from holster friction, minor impact marks on the canister from belt mounting, and occasional tooling residue around the pressure gauge. Security teams rarely maintain cosmetic condition; functional integrity is the only metric.
